_comment: Append-only price table. Each row is a PRICE OBSERVATION with the date it was true and where it came from -- never edited in place. Cost for a historical lane row is derived by joining on (model, effective_from <= lane.ts < next effective_from). A lane row that stores only a computed total_cost_usd is unreadable once prices move; store raw token counts and join here.

REFRESH CADENCE. Do not poll daily. For any provider that reports cost per call (Claude does, via `claude -p --output-format json` -> total_cost_usd), no cadence is needed: every lane row stores BOTH observed_cost_usd and derived_cost_usd (raw tokens priced against this table), and a divergence between them IS the price-change alarm. It fires on the next run anyone happens to make, costs nothing, and cannot go stale between checks. Reconcile, do not poll. For a provider that reports tokens but NOT cost (codex exec), there is nothing to reconcile against, so that side needs an explicit check: at model-id launch or change, at a CLI upgrade window (the fleet already gates those), and a monthly floor as backstop. Triggers beat calendars everywhere except where reconciliation is impossible.
